memory_update.text: For the leading-edge foundry/equipment node, prioritize direct research on TSM, ASML, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC before moving to second-order suppliers such as test, EDA/IP, materials, gases, and subsystems.
The node appears to split into at least four sub-chokepoints: advanced-node wafer capacity, EUV/High-NA lithography, etch/deposition/materials engineering, and process-control/yield management.

This pass did not include semiconductor test leaders such as Teradyne or Advantest, EDA/IP leaders such as Synopsys/Cadence/Arm, or materials/gases suppliers; those should be covered in a separate Layer 1B pass if the node is widened beyond foundry and core wafer-fab equipment.
Need a follow-up evidence pass focused on export-control exposure, China revenue concentration, backlog quality, shipment lead times, and capex-cycle timing for ASML, AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC.

node: Leading-edge foundry capacity and semiconductor equipment
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the leading-edge foundry and semiconductor equipment node. The highest-direct-exposure candidates are TSMC as the leading advanced-node foundry/advanced-packaging asset owner, ASML as the EUV lithography chokepoint, and Applied Materials, Lam Research, and KLA as major wafer-fab equipment and process-control suppliers tied to leading-edge logic, DRAM/HBM, advanced packaging, and yield learning. This is a research universe only, not a buy/sell list.
